parts.text:
Now use all the given information:
1. model.json file
2. operation.json file
3. Multiview images

Decide which sections of the original model should be modified, removed, interacted with or if new sections should be created. Use as much information from the Multiview images, model.json files and operation.json as possible.

Make this decision from several perspectives. If target clearly identify geometry, locate the corresponding section(s) and face(s) in model.json. If there is no clear geometry identified, use the referenced features and relational_constraint to identify potential sections and features. Additionally, consider the intention of the edit. Based on the function and behavior associated with each section and features, decide which section require the action the most. Then, find the corresponding section and face code from model.json.

Plan out the modeling procedure needed to perform each action. Describe them in professional CAD modelling languages from choosing the plane, draw sketches to extrusion, add chamfers. Be thorough and detailed.

face_code values in model.json are visual labels from shaded renders. Brep_id is the CadQuery Faces() index from the STEP analysis report (for example FACE 0).

Edit operation.json accordingly. Keep the previous request_wording and actions, and add localization plus steps.

OUTPUT FORMAT (JSON, operation.json, no markdown fences, use this schema):
{
  "request": "",
  "request_wording": {
    "action_words": ["..."],
    "referenced_feature_words": ["..."],
    "intention_words": ["..."],
    "grammatical_words": ["..."]
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "operation": "...",
      "parameters": {
        "parameter_name": "..."
      },
      "target": "...",
      "relational_constraint": "...",
      "unresolved_reference": "...",
      "target section code": ["..."],
      "target face code": ["..."],
      "steps": [
        "...",
        "..."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "intention": ["..."]
}

The model.json, operation.json, and labeled multi-view images follow.

{
  "request": "If edge with bigger radius is considered as top, add supporting structure to the bottom of the frame by offseting inner wall by 2cm with thickness of 0,5cm of the supporting structure all around. This will create step at the bottom of the frame, enlarging bottom surface area. Leave out radii at the bottom edges. Add radii from top, 0,2cm which will create smoothe transition from above. Bottom remains flat.",
  "request_wording": {
    "action_words": [
      "add",
      "supporting",
      "structure",
      "offseting",
      "2cm",
      "thickness",
      "0,5cm",
      "create",
      "step",
      "Leave",
      "out",
      "radii",
      "Add",
      "radii",
      "0,2cm",
      "create",
      "flat"
    ],
    "referenced_feature_words": [
      "edge",
      "bigger",
      "radius",
      "top",
      "bottom",
      "frame",
      "inner",
      "wall",
      "around",
      "bottom",
      "surface",
      "area",
      "bottom",
      "edges",
      "top",
      "transition",
      "above",
      "Bottom"
    ],
    "intention_words": [
      "enlarging",
      "smoothe"
    ],
    "grammatical_words": [
      "If",
      "with",
      "is",
      "considered",
      "as",
      "to",
      "the",
      "of",
      "the",
      "by",
      "by",
      "with",
      "of",
      "of",
      "the",
      "all",
      "This",
      "will",
      "at",
      "the",
      "of",
      "the",
      "which",
      "will",

      "from",

    ]
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "operation": "Define/confirm model orientation such that the side associated with the edge having the bigger existing radius is treated as the top (thereby identifying the bottom as the opposite side).",
      "parameters": {},
      "target": "Existing edge(s) that have radii; overall part orientation (top vs bottom).",
      "relational_constraint": "Top is the side corresponding to the edge with the bigger radius.",
      "unresolved_reference": "Which specific edge(s) have the bigger radius, and whether there are multiple candidates requiring a unique top definition."
    },
    {
      "operation": "Create a continuous supporting step/ledge feature at the bottom of the frame by offsetting the inner wall profile and forming material with the stated thickness all around.",
      "parameters": {
        "offset_distance": "2cm",
        "support_structure_thickness": "0,5cm"
      },
      "target": "Bottom region of the frame, referenced from the inner wall perimeter/profile.",
      "relational_constraint": "Feature is on the bottom of the frame (opposite the identified top) and runs all around (continuous around the full perimeter). Bottom should remain flat.",
      "unresolved_reference": "Exact offset direction relative to the inner wall (inward vs outward), what 'thickness' refers to (vertical height vs radial/normal thickness), and the specific faces/edges that define the 'inner wall' and bottom datum/plane for the step."
    },
    {
      "operation": "Remove or avoid applying radii/fillets on the bottom edges of the frame/added supporting step so bottom edges remain sharp.",
      "parameters": {},
      "target": "Bottom edges (edges bounding the bottom face and/or bottom of the new step) of the frame/supporting structure.",
      "relational_constraint": "No radii at bottom edges; preserve a flat bottom condition.",
      "unresolved_reference": "Which bottom edges currently have fillets/radii (if any) and which specific edge loops should be kept sharp after the modification."
    },
    {
      "operation": "Apply fillets (radii) of the specified size to the top-side edges of the new supporting step to create a smooth transition from above without affecting the bottom.",
      "parameters": {
        "fillet_radius": "0,2cm"
      },
      "target": "Top edges of the supporting structure/step (i.e., the edges on the upper side of the added feature where it transitions to the existing frame geometry).",
      "relational_constraint": "Fillets are applied from the top side only to smooth the transition from above; bottom remains flat; do not add radii to bottom edges.",
      "unresolved_reference": "Which exact edges constitute 'from top' (upper edge loop(s) of the step) and how to limit the fillet propagation so the bottom face/edges remain unaffected."
    }
  ],
  "intention": [
    "Add a supporting structure at the bottom of the frame.",
    "Create a bottom step to enlarge the bottom surface area.",
    "Maintain a flat bottom while providing a smooth transition from the upper side via small top-side radii."
  ]
}
